text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In 1940, during World War II, Germany rented 500 goods wagons from Sweden to export coal and coke from Germany to Sweden but it is not clear what the wagons were used for. Most of them were never returned to Sweden. In 1950, 275 wagons were still missing and the ones returned were damaged.
- Automotive group AB Volvo's chief executive's decision to step down could mean a more intense pace for cooperation within several of Volvo's operations.

- No Swedish minister openly supports a Swedish membership in Europe's planned Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), according to a survey done by the newspaper. The few ministers with a positive view on membership say they have not made a final decision on their position.

- Chief executive of Electrolux, Leif Johansson, will move back to his home town of Gothenburg to replace Soren Gyll as head of Swedish automotive group AB Volvo. Johansson, chief executive of Electrolux, will in April take over as CEO of Volvo, replacing Soren Gyll who will step down. Atlas Copco head Michael Treschow will fill Johansson's shoes, while Atlas Copco's Giulio Mazzalupi will replace Treschow.

- The fact that one of the chief executives in the Wallenberg family's financial empire, Electrolux's Johansson, steps into Volvo is no power conspiracy but merely shows that Sweden is a small country, according to a paper column.

- Swedish defence minister Thage Peterson on Monday turned against the Swedish defence and defence industry by saying the entire quarrel about Volvo Aero's decision to close down its plant in Arboga, Sweden, is an organised campaign against the government's defence policies.

- Three of Sweden's largest exporting companies - automotive group AB Volvo, household appliance group Electrolux AB and engineering group Atlas Copco AB - all announced on Monday that they will switch chief executives.
- Swedish construction company Skanska AB won an order worth $129 million to renovate a bridge in New York. The contract will be shared with New York company NAB.

- The value of Sweden's exports to central and eastern Europe increased by four percent to 15.5 billion crowns during the first ten months of 1996, compared to the corresponding part of 1995, according to national statistics agency SCB.
